result.title: Depth as a Candidate Source: Portfolio Allocation for Recurrent Test-Time Scaling in Large Language Models
result.summary: Recurrent latent reasoning in large lanugage models (LLMs) scales test-time computation by increasing recurrent depth, naturally framing inference as a problem of deciding when to stop. We identify a previously overlooked limitation of this single-depth view through systematic preliminary analysis: deeper recurrence can lose correct solutions found at shallower depths, while depth-specific success sets remain broadly non-nested even after controlling for marginal accuracy. This suggests that depth determines not only computation cost, but also access to distinct candidate solutions. Motivated by this finding, we propose Depth Portfolio Allocation (DPA), which reformulates recurrent test-time scaling as budgeted allocation across depth-specific candidate sources. DPA supports both fixed portfolios and feedback-guided sequential allocation under a shared inference budget. Experiments on GSM8K, SVAMP, MultiArith, and MBPP show that mixed-depth portfolios expand oracle coverage under matched candidate counts and nominal costs, while feedback-guided allocation generally matches or improves uniform allocation and can reduce computation in high-budget settings. Code and data are avaible at : https://anonymous.4open.science/r/LLM-latent-B7BC/.

AI.brief_summary: 论文通过初步分析发现循环 latent 推理中不同 recurrent depth 的成功集合并不嵌套、更深层会丢掉浅层已得出的正确答案，据此提出 Depth Portfolio Allocation，把测试时计算重述为多深度候选源之间的预算分配，并比较固定组合与反馈引导的顺序分配，在 GSM8K、SVAMP、MultiArith、MBPP 上考察 oracle 覆盖与计算成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及 latent 循环推理的深度—停止决策与计算预算问题，「深度不仅是成本、还决定可访问的候选解」这一结论可供核查 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的支持组合与多层状态复用；但实验限于纯文本任务，其与视觉证据筛选的关联需读原文确认。
